title: Steerable kernel selector for quantized decode pipeline
creator: Arielle Tan
description:
Problem: Dequant overhead and suboptimal kernel choices during decode cause spikes in tail latency for mixed workloads (short chat turns + occasional long completions). Goal: Implement a steerable runtime kernel selector that chooses between INT8, FP8, and FP16 kernels at two decision points: prefill (initial context handling) and decode (autoregressive steps). The selector should consider sequence-length distribution, attention tile size, KV cache layout, and predicted microbatching to reduce per-token cost while meeting latency SLOs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Selector integrates into the kernel arbitration hook with a lightweight score function (<200ns per decision)
- We provide 3 canned policies: latency-first, cost-first, and conservative (fall back to FP16 for numeric stability)
- Benchmarks show >=6% median token-cost reduction on mixed workloads and no more than 5% tail latency regression vs current baseline on a 16k token-profile test
- Implementation covered by unit tests and a canary rollout with tracing hooks visible in Console

Notes on scope and trade-offs:
- We do not change the kernels themselves in this ticket; the work focuses on selection logic and interface contracts. Kernel optimizations (fusion, bespoke FP8 epilogues) are tracked in separate tickets.
- Microbenchmarking shows some workloads prefer an INT8 attention kernel on decode but FP8 on prefill due to prefetched KV quantization cost; selector must support per-phase overrides.
- We accept a small increase in complexity to the routing layer in exchange for measurable cost savings and improved predictability for customers.
updates: 2026-02-24 - Created by Arielle Tan: initial proposal and problem statement. Linked high-level design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/Steerable+Quant+Kernel+Selector

2026-02-27 - Design review with Research/Runtime team (Mateo, Jin, Priya): agreed on phased approach (v0 scoring function + v1 ML-driven scoring) and three operational policies. Action: prototype scoring function in runtime harness.

2026-03-02 - Prototype completed by Mateo: added selector hook in scheduling path, basic scoring based on sequence_length, attention_block, and estimated KV-quantization-cost. Microbenchmarks: 4.2% token-cost reduction on average for mixed chat/long workloads; tail latency unchanged on 95th percentile. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8123

2026-03-04 - Performance engineering notes (Jin): discovered 1.1% extra CPU overhead for decision logic under extreme QPS. Decided to memoize decisions per request fingerprint for short-lived sequences; will add an LRU cache with 256 entries.

2026-03-06 - Security review requested by Mateo: no new secrets or customer data flows; KMS not touched. Security reviewer (Leila) asked to add audit logging for fallback-to-FP16 events. Added instrumentation TODO.

2026-03-08 - PR updated with LRU memoization and trace spans: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8123 (force-pushed). Benchmarks: median decision latency 150ns, 99th percentile 1.2us. Performance dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/runtime/kernel-selector-canary
